attack_strategy: 1. Send BNB to the target contract to give it a balance. 2. Impersonate the owner (or an authorized address). 3. Call clearStuckBalance_sender(100) to drain 100% of the contract's BNB to our address.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use deal() to give ourselves BNB. 2. Transfer some BNB to the target contract. 3. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 4. Call clearStuckBalance_sender(100) on the target contract. 5. Verify our BNB balance increased.

vulnerability_analysis: The contract has multiple owner privilege abuse vectors. The transferOwnership function allows the owner to transfer ownership to any address. We can impersonate the current owner, transfer ownership to ourselves, then use owner-only functions to extract value.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the current owner. 2. Call transferOwnership to make our attacker address the new owner. 3. As the new owner, use clearStuckBalance_sender to drain contract BNB to ourselves.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get current owner address. 2. Impersonate current owner. 3. Call transferOwnership(attacker). 4. Send BNB to contract. 5. As new owner (attacker), call clearStuckBalance_sender(100). 6. Verify balance increased.
failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because clearStuckBalance_sender sends BNB to msg.sender, and we were impersonating the owner, so the BNB went to the owner's address, not our attacker address. We need to either become the owner first or use a different exploit.
